edits.find:
A hard painless mass near a joint with a bony spur whose cortex and medulla run continuously into the parent bone is an osteochondroma, the most common benign bone tumor. Its natural course is to grow with the skeleton until the physis closes, then stay put. Management is observation.

Every wrong option is another tumor's natural course. Spontaneous involution belongs to osteoid osteoma. Pathological fracture from medullary expansion belongs to the unicameral bone cyst, which hollows the shaft from within. Aggressive cortical destruction belongs to the epiphyseal pair, chondroblastoma and giant cell tumor. Malignant transformation to chondrosarcoma is real but around 1% for a solitary lesion, so it is the thing to counsel about rather than the expected course.

A painful lytic lesion in the pelvis of a teenager with fever is Ewing sarcoma. It peaks at age 10 to 15, favors the diaphysis, pelvis and axial skeleton, and can bring fever, leukocytosis and high ESR and CRP, so it is mistaken for osteomyelitis; systemic findings often mean it has already spread. The film shows a permeative lytic lesion with onion-skin periosteal layers, and biopsy shows sheets of small round blue cells. Osteosarcoma is the more common adolescent bone cancer, but it sits in a long-bone metaphysis, rarely the pelvis, and systemic findings are rare. Osteomyelitis usually seeds a long-bone metaphysis rather than the ilium, and its biopsy shows inflammatory cells and necrotic bone. Leukemia causes bone pain by marrow expansion without a lytic lesion. Chondrosarcoma is the pelvic tumor of adults over 40 to 50.

edits.find:
A teenager presents with progressive thoracic kyphosis. The question gives you one exam move: does the curve correct when the patient lies prone or on hyperextension? A curve that corrects is postural roundback; a curve that does not correct is structural. When the kyphosis is rigid and the lateral spine film shows anterior wedging ≥5° in ≥3 consecutive vertebrae, the diagnosis is Scheuermann disease. Schmorl nodes (disc herniation through the endplate) support the diagnosis but are not required.

Pattern-matching “teenager with kyphosis” to postural roundback without running the correction test is the miss. The fix is a single exam finding: ask “does it correct?” before naming the disease.

edits.find:
An acute hot, swollen, erythematous joint with severe pain on passive range of motion and fever gets aspirated — and the reason is stronger than "this looks septic."
